I never even was diagnosed, but I could fill pages upon pages of emotional shit I've felt since I was young and the progression of said shit. I began writing at a young age, and granted it was mostly angsty shit about my depression, it was my own and I didn't want that to go. Poe and Hemmingway dealt with that shit, I figured I could to if I tried.

I didn't realize it at first, but writing was the first step in combating my issues. You need a creative hobby. Something you can use to create a physical manifestation of yourself in a way. Some would say it is a distraction, but art helps you discover yourself, as fruity as that sounds. But don't do it with the idea of becoming big or something, do it for yourself. Because you'll come to see you have something to offer, a story to tell, a song to sing.

You'll become proud in a way, and you can use this pride to see there's good in you, and that conclusion will lead you to other good things about you.

In terms of treatment with outside things, try natural things. Hiking, tea, and I hate to sound like a stoner but marijuana (in moderation). Even reasonable vices can help when used properly. I avoid alcohol because it is after all, a depresant, but whatever vices you have should be both embraced and moderated (obviously don't do coke, bang strippers and gamble your shirt off, but you catch my drift).

In the end, the brain operates on a risk-reward system. When the risk of living seems too intolerable, suicidal thoughts happen. But you have to come to the conclusion that life can only get better, and that even if humans have paved over what's around you the world itself is a beautiful, breathtaking place. My end-all was that I want to see it, I want to see as much as I can before I go and if I go then I don't get to see it for myself. Even if I want to kill myself sometimes still, I'm still me, and that goal prevents me from offing myself should all else fail. And besides, even if that isn't enough, and your life just gets too toxic, the possibility of picking up and leaving everything behind to wander is always there and at least gives you the chance for things to change. Everywhere is different. You can always kill trillneato but you can stay alive a someone else.

What I'm getting at is there are thousands of alternatives to try, so many that you can't even try them all before you die, and you owe it to yourself to at least try them.

I rambled a bit, but I hope I didn't detract too far.
